templateNote: A comparison reads best as: why, the options side by side (a table), each option's trade-offs, the criteria, the evidence, and the decision status. The criteria and the options stay in different frames, and the decision frame names no winner.

frames.title: Why the billing queue is changing
frames.purpose: The problem the comparison solves and the load it must carry.
frames.rationale: Context is separate from the options; it explains the first must-have.

frames.title: Three options compared
frames.purpose: The three options with their monthly costs and effort, side by side.
frames.rationale: A cost comparison across options is tabular: one row per option, one column per figure.

separateFrom.reason: The criteria judge the options; mixing them reads as if a criterion were a property of one option.

frames.title: Trade-offs by option
frames.purpose: Each option's benefit with the conditions and costs that come with it.
frames.rationale: Grouping trade-offs by option, side by side, lets the reader compare like with like.

frames.title: Selection criteria
frames.purpose: The two must-haves that gate options and the weights that score the rest.
frames.rationale: Criteria apply to every option, so they get their own frame.

frames.title: Evidence so far
frames.purpose: What has been measured, and what has not.
frames.rationale: Evidence is kept apart from claims so the reader can see that only one option was tested.

frames.title: Decision status: deferred
frames.purpose: That no option is chosen, what the decision waits for, and the next step.
frames.rationale: The note's conclusion is a deferral; it needs its own frame so it isn't read as a recommendation.

elements.content: In-process workers lose queued jobs on deploys and crashes (37 invoice emails last quarter); about 40,000 jobs a day, peak 600 a minute
One row per option: what it is, monthly infrastructure ($310 / $540 / $0 extra), monthly team effort (about 2 / 12 / 4 hours), with the volume assumption and the broker's estimate noted on their rows
elements.layout: A table, not three cards: the figures are compared across rows.

elements.content: Managed queue: almost no operational work and automatic dead-lettering — but at-least-once delivery means every handler must be idempotent first (only the email handler is today); provider lock-in
Self-hosted broker: priority queues and delayed delivery — but upgrades need a maintenance window
Job table: enqueue in the same transaction as the billing change — only for jobs inside the billing database transaction (not the reporting service's); polling loads the primary at month-end
Must-haves: no job lost on a crash or deploy; 1,800 jobs per minute without manual intervention. Failing either rules an option out
Weighted criteria: operational effort 40%, monthly cost 30%, developer experience 20%, portability 10%
Job table load test: 1,200 jobs a minute at p95 18 ms; at 2,000 a minute CPU 85% and p95 240 ms — 1,800 not tested, staging a quarter of production size
Managed queue and broker were not load-tested; the managed queue's throughput is the provider's figure

No option is recommended: the decision waits for the job table measured at 1,800 jobs a minute on a production-sized database. Open requirement per option: idempotent handlers / a broker owner / a passing load test
Priya: bring the load-test result to the next architecture review

relationships.explanation: The load test is the evidence about the job table's load on the primary database.
The decision waits on the measurement the load test did not make.
The 1,800 a minute the decision waits for is the throughput must-have.

together.reason: Trade-offs are compared side by side, one card per option.

keepSeparate.reason: Criteria judge the options; they are not one more row or column of the comparison.
The no-lost-jobs must-have is not Option C's benefit, even though Option C addresses it; merging them pre-judges the decision.
The decision status sits apart from any one option so it can't be read as that option's verdict.

hierarchy.reason: The load test is evidence about the job table's polling load, not a co-equal option.

unsupported.ideal: Each card cites its units: table u6–u15, u28; trade-offs u24–u32 (minus u28); criteria u16–u23; evidence u33–u38; status u39–u45.
unsupported.expectedToday: Not checkable; matching is by content.

unsupported.ideal: Evidence cards and criteria cards are styled distinctly from option cards.
unsupported.expectedToday: Plain cards; frames carry the distinction.
